title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'Deuxième partie' studies algebraic-group models attached to the modular group SL2(Z), generated by the elliptic elements ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4). T_ρ and T_σ are presumably the rank-2 centralizer tori Res G_m of ρ and σ in GL2. N'_σ is the normalizer of T_σ, with sign character ε: N'_σ → μ2 whose kernel is T_σ. T_0 is a further torus. M_{ρ,σ} is a group acting on SG (≈ SL2-type), and its centre was reduced on p.408 to the centre of an extension Γ_{ρ,σ} of μ2×μ2 by a commutative group Γ°.

This page computes that centre. Write 𝒯 = SG*_{ρ,σ}(∞) ⊂ G_{ρ,σ}(∞) ≅ T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ. The map (u,a,b) ↦ (ε(b), det a/det u) gives an exact sequence 1→𝒯°→𝒯→μ2×μ2→1 (labelled (48)). It maps to 1→T_0×T_ρ×T_σ→T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ→μ2→1, compatibly with the first projection μ2×μ2→μ2.

Since 𝒯° is commutative, conjugation induces an action of μ2×μ2 on it. The diagram shows this action factors through the first factor. The nontrivial element acts trivially on T_0×T_ρ and on T_σ by the canonical 'conjugation' σ ↦ εσ. So the invariants are cut out by T_0×T_ρ×G_m (scalars are the conjugation-invariants of T_σ).

More generally, let 𝒯' = Ker(𝒯→μ2), (u,a,b) ↦ ε(b). It lies in the commutative group T_0×T_ρ×T_σ. Hence the trace (intersection) of the centre of 𝒯 on 𝒯' is the trace of T_0×T_ρ×G_m on 𝒯'.

Finally, μ2 acts faithfully on T_σ, and 𝒯' maps epimorphically onto T_σ. So μ2 acts faithfully on 𝒯', and no element with ε(b) = −1 is central. Thus Centre(𝒯) ⊂ 𝒯' = Ker(𝒯→μ2), giving Centre(𝒯) = 𝒯 ∩ (T_0×T_ρ×G_m). This is summarized as (49) on the next page. That page then extracts the part acting trivially on SG and finds the finite group Z/6×Z/2×Z/2 of integral points in the modular case.
errors: Notation drift: p.408 identifies Γ°_{ρ,σ} with G*_{ρ,σ}(0), here the group is called SG*_{ρ,σ}(∞) and written 𝒯; also N^0_σ in the lower row should be T_σ (kernel of ε). No mathematical error found; the argument (commutative kernel + faithful action of the outer μ2 ⇒ centre lies in the kernel and equals the invariants) is correct.

ideas.what: Centre of an extension of a finite group by a commutative group scheme computed as the invariants of the induced action, plus the observation that the faithfully acting coset contributes nothing to the centre
ideas.modern_name: centre of an extension / fixed points of outer action; Galois-conjugation invariants of a norm torus Res_{K/Q}G_m are G_m

ideas.what: Algebraic-group (torus/normalizer) models T_ρ, N'_σ attached to the elliptic generators of the modular group, used to compute centres of groups M_{ρ,σ} in the study of the 'équation des lacets'
ideas.modern_name: centralizer tori and normalizers of elliptic elements in GL2; related to Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations for PSL2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's program (Esquisse); later Drinfeld, Ihara for GT
ideas.where_published: context only: Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche discuss the modular group and Teichmüller tower, not this computation

deep.surprise_reason: A routine centre computation inside a longer unpublished calculation; correct, but it contains no new idea or connection a specialist would find notable.
transcription_corrections: 'montre, plus généralement, que le tore ... est aussi le tore' should read 'que la trace du centre de 𝒯_{ρ,σ} sur le sous-groupe 𝒯'_{ρ,σ} de 𝒯_{ρ,σ} noyau de ... est aussi la trace, sur ce sous-groupe, de T_0×T_ρ×G_m'.
'(qui est plat s'envoie épimorphiquement sur T_σ)' should read '(qui en effet s'envoie épimorphiquement sur T_σ)'.
Lower row of diagram: 'T_0×T_ρ×N^0_σ' is T_0×T_ρ×N°_σ = T_0×T_ρ×T_σ; the vertical arrow on μ2×μ2 is labelled 'première proj'.
'506' at top is Grothendieck's own pagination; '409' is the archive folio.
